question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the norm of the vector $x$ in terms of $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{k}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9+{k}^{2}+16} \\  & =\sqrt{{k}^{2}+29}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $‖x‖=3\sqrt{6},$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{k}^{2}+29} & =3\sqrt{6} \\ {(\sqrt{{k}^{2}+29})}^{2} & ={(3\sqrt{6})}^{2} \\ {k}^{2}+29 & =9\cdot 6 \\ {k}^{2}+29 & =54 \\ {k}^{2} & =25 \\ k & =\pm 5\end{aligned}
$$
